battle.name: 第三次馬其頓戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前171至168年，第三次馬其頓戰爭是羅馬借仲裁塞琉古王位糾紛之機、攻滅馬其頓王國的戰爭。168年6月22日，兩軍在皮德納決戰：馬其頓方陣正面未崩，卻因右翼指揮官陣亡、側翼遭輕步兵與騎兵衝撞而瓦解。卡面秦弩不在此戰現場，卻是同時代東亞的對應物：秦國以弩機配給北方邊防步兵，在塹壕後壓制匈奴騎兵。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 第三次馬其頓戰爭（公元前171至168年）表面上是一場由羅馬仲裁塞琉古王位繼承而引起的戰爭，實際上決定了希臘化世界最後一個獨立王國的存亡。羅馬一方是執政官與元老院：執政官在任內須先以「特使」身分赴希臘執行任務，戰事爆發後再以帶兵的執政官身分進入戰場；兵員由羅馬軍團、社會戰後編入的意大利同盟軍團，以及盟邦提供的輔助部隊組成，兩支三列槳戰艦的艦隊負責封鎖愛琴海北岸與馬其頓沿岸的海路，埃托利亞同盟、帕加馬王國、帖撒利同盟與亞該亞人先後派兵助羅馬；站在珀耳修斯一方的有色雷斯的奧德里西王國、摩羅索斯人、阿塔曼尼亞人與克里特援軍，伊利里亞王國的根提烏斯原是羅馬盟友，公元前169年改投馬其頓。塞琉古一方是安提柯王朝的塞琉古王國，此時深陷安提柯四世死後的內戰，只掌握東部領土，能派出的援軍規模有限，真正能提供地面部隊的是馬其頓王國。馬其頓國王珀耳修斯站在塞琉古一方，但他的營內並不團結：一批「計算派」臣僚主張先與羅馬討價還價，另一批人則認定羅馬的仲裁書等於一紙亡國令，於是擁護國王全面開戰。羅馬之所以選在馬其頓開刀而不直接攻塞琉古本土，是因為塞琉古太大、離得太遠，而馬其頓小、位置好、又已經站到羅馬的對面；拿下馬其頓，等於拔掉塞琉古伸向希臘的一根手指頭。
countriesEn: The Third Macedonian War (171-168 BC) began on the surface as a war provoked by Roman arbitration over the Seleucid succession, but in reality it decided the survival of the last independent kingdom of the Hellenistic world. On the Roman side stood the consuls and the Senate of the republic: a consul in office first had to travel to Greece on special assignment, and only after the fighting began did he enter the field as a consular commander; the troops were Roman legions, Italian allied formations incorporated after the Social War, and contingents supplied by allied states, while two fleets of triremes blockaded the northern Aegean and the coast of Macedonia so that no relief could land. The Aetolian League, the kingdom of Pergamon, the Thessalian League and the Achaeans sent troops to Rome's side; on Perseus's side stood the Odrysian kingdom of Thrace, the Molossians, the Athamanians and Cretan contingents, while Gentius the Illyrian king, originally Rome's ally, changed sides to Macedon in 169 BC. On the Seleucid side stood the Seleucid Empire of the Antigonid dynasty, then deep in civil war after the death of Antiochus IV: it held only the eastern provinces and could field limited reinforcements, and the power that really supplied ground troops was the kingdom of Macedon. King Perseus of Macedon lined up with the Seleucids, but his own camp was not united: one group of 'calculating' courtiers argued for haggling with Rome first, while another group held that the Roman award was already a death warrant for the kingdom and therefore backed the king in open war. Rome chose to strike at Macedon rather than invade Seleucid territory directly because Seleucid Syria was too large and too far away, whereas Macedon was small, well placed, and had already lined up on Rome's opposite side. Taking Macedon meant cutting off one of the fingers that Seleucid power extended into Greece.
people: 核心人物是馬其頓國王珀耳修斯。他是安提柯王朝的遠支，約公元前179年即位，起初只是先王倚重的「計算派」諸臣手上的傀儡，娶塞琉古王女，又在塞琉古王位繼承的仲裁中押注德米特里二世，卻在公元前171年被羅馬的仲裁書判定為「無資格爭位」。同年他派兄弟德米特里赴羅馬陳情，羅馬把德米特里扣在亞得里亞海彼岸當作人質，斷了王室向外求援的線；珀耳修斯隨即調集軍隊、開放邊境，讓約一萬名羅馬軍隊毫無抵抗地進入馬其頓南部，從而把自己從「仲裁當事人」變成「羅馬的敵人」。羅馬方面的指揮序列可以逐一對上：公元前171年由執政官普布利烏斯·李奇尼烏斯·克拉蘇領軍，公元前170年換上奧魯斯·霍斯特利烏斯·曼奇努斯，公元前169年由昆圖斯·馬爾基烏斯·菲利普斯接手，公元前168年才是取勝的盧基烏斯·埃米利烏斯·保利那·馬其頓尼庫斯，他堅持休整與整備，把遠征軍練成可野戰、可攻城的樣子；此外還有真正拍板的元老院，它派遣由奧克塔維烏斯、梅魯拉與馬切多組成的使團出任裁判。馬其頓方面除國王之外，還有國王之弟德米特里、國王之子菲力普、統率騎兵的米尼翁、埃托利亞人阿爾刻德莫斯、色雷斯的奧德里西王科提斯四世，以及改投馬其頓的伊利里亞王根提烏斯；皮德納會戰當日，菲力普與德米特里相繼陣亡，國王本人只帶數千騎兵突圍。塞琉古一方的安提柯四世已死，真正的棋手是在羅馬與塞琉古之間往來的謀臣索西比烏斯，以及帕加馬王歐梅尼斯二世——他是羅馬最重要的盟友，卻也代表羅馬對安提柯家族的敵意，因為他本人就是安提柯四世的宿敵。
peopleEn: The central figure was Perseus, king of Macedon, a distant branch of the Antigonid house who took the throne about 179 BC. At first he was little more than the puppet of the 'calculating' ministers who had supported his father; he married a Seleucid princess, backed Demetrius II in the Seleucid succession, and in 171 BC was judged by the Roman award to have no claim to the Seleucid throne at all. That same year he sent his brother Demetrius to Rome with pleas, and the Romans kept Demetrius on the far side of the Adriatic as a hostage, cutting the royal house off from any appeal abroad. Perseus then mustered troops and opened his borders, letting about ten thousand Romans walk into southern Macedon without resistance, and so turned himself from a party to an arbitration into an enemy of Rome. The Roman command sequence can be matched year by year: Publius Licinius Crassus led in 171 BC, Aulus Hostilius Mancinus took over in 170, Quintus Marcius Philippus in 169, and only in 168 came Lucius Aemilius Paullus Macedonicus, who won, insisting on rest and reorganisation and turning the expeditionary army into a force that could fight in the field and lay siege; above them all sat the Senate, which dispatched a tribunal of envoys - Gnaeus Octavius, Gnaeus Cornelius Merula and Lucius Aemilius Macedo - to act as judges. On the Macedonian side, besides the king, stood his brother Demetrius, his son Philippus, Minnion who commanded the cavalry, the Aetolian Archedemus, Cotys IV of the Odrysian kingdom in Thrace, and Gentius the Illyrian king who had changed sides; on the day of Pydna Philippus and Demetrius were killed in turn and the king escaped with only a few thousand horsemen. On the Seleucid side Antiochus IV was already dead, and the real hand was played by Sosibius, the minister who moved between the Seleucid court and Rome, and by Eumenes II of Pergamon, Rome's most valuable ally, who at the same time embodied Rome's hatred of the Antigonid house, being the sworn enemy of Antiochus IV.
kits: 卡面這件秦弩在皮德納的戰場上並不存在，這點必須先講清楚：公元前二世紀的希臘世界沒有中國式的金屬機牙弩機，希臘化軍隊的投射兵器是弓、標槍，以及工程用的弩砲與野驢砲，皆由受過訓練的工程兵操作；卡利尼庫斯一役馬其頓人還試用一種新造的投槍（cestrosphendone），以雙股皮條的投索甩出，羅馬方面則以象兵應對；馬其頓與塞琉古的步兵用薩里沙長矛與小圓盾，方陣是他們的骨幹，希臘化王國真正的攻城技術是配重式與扭力式弩砲。相反，秦弩的技術路徑完全不同：它把拉力存進金屬機牙，射手不必像拉弓那樣把弦拉到耳邊，因此可以在掩體後、把弩機架在牆頭、樹上或車板上，並且連續射擊；從戰國到秦，弩是中國步兵的主要射程兵器，出土秦簡裏有對弩機、弩箭規格與登記的規定，說明秦國把弩當成可點驗、可補充的制式裝備，北方防線上的秦軍正是靠大量弩兵在塹壕、關塞後面壓制匈奴騎兵。就本役的戰術位置而言，秦弩相當於希臘人「弩砲」在攻城中的作用，只不過一個守、一個攻；而與它同場對位的羅馬步兵用的是軟柄重標槍、短劍與大盾，馬其頓方陣用薩里沙，羅馬的馬其頓式中心騎兵、努米底亞騎兵與克里特弓手負責側翼迂回，另有努米底亞王馬西尼薩之子米西阿熱涅斯帶來的二十頭象。羅馬的攻城裝備包括撞錘、攻城塔、木橋與壕溝，與希臘人的弩砲同樣屬於前四至前三世紀工程技術的產物。馬其頓方面還有一項常被忽略的裝備問題：方陣長矛需要極大空間，與騎兵混編時必須拉開距離，這正是皮德納敗局的物理原因。
kitsEn: The Chinese crossbow on this card was not present on the field at Pydna, and that has to be said plainly: the Greek world of the second century BC had no Chinese-style metal-trigger crossbow. The missile weapons of Hellenistic armies were the bow, the javelin, and above all siege artillery - the catapult and the onager - worked by trained engineers; at Callinicus the Macedonians also tried a newly invented dart, the cestrosphendone, slung from a two-thonged cord, and the Romans answered with elephants; Macedonian and Seleucid infantry carried the sarissa and small round shields, the phalanx was the core of their armies, and the real siege technology of the Hellenistic kingdoms was the counterweight and torsion artillery. The Chinese crossbow followed a different technical path: it stored the drawn power in a metal trigger mechanism, so the archer never had to hold the string back to his ear, which meant it could be fired from behind cover, from a wall top, from a tree or from a cart bed, and fired repeatedly. From the Warring States period to the Qin, the crossbow was the principal ranged arm of Chinese infantry; excavated Qin legal texts contain regulations on the specification and the registration of crossbow mechanisms and bolts, which shows that the Qin state treated the crossbow as a standard piece of equipment that could be inspected and replenished, and it was Qin crossbowmen massed behind ramparts and passes who held down Xiongnu cavalry on the northern frontier. As for the tactical position of the crossbow in this war, it corresponds roughly to what the artillery did for the Greeks in siege operations, except that one defends and the other attacks. The equipment actually opposite it on the field of Pydna was Roman: the soft-shanked heavy javelin, the pilum, the short sword, the large shield, the skirmishing javelin of the velites, and cavalry for the flank - the Roman turmae of centre-horse, Numidian horsemen and Cretan archers - plus twenty elephants brought over by Misagenes, son of Masinissa king of Numidia. Roman siege equipment included the battering ram, the siege tower, the wooden boarding bridge and the ditch, products of exactly the same engineering-technical ferment as the Greek catapults of the fourth and third centuries BC. One more Macedonian equipment problem is often overlooked: the sarissa needs a great deal of room, and it must be spaced well apart from cavalry, which is the physical reason for the Macedonian defeat at Pydna.
tactics: 第三次馬其頓戰爭的戰術可以分成三段。公元前171年，羅馬軍越過亞得里亞海，在馬其頓山區行軍時被狼群咬傷士兵，軍中視為不祥；真正決定作戰節奏的是達伊尼洛斯山口那條狹窄通道，羅馬軍以縱隊行軍，行李隊與後衛遭到馬其頓輕騎劫掠，羅馬用正面縱隊與騎兵掩護硬推過去，才取得進逼王都的通道。同年稍後在卡利尼庫斯河一役，馬其頓人試用新造的投槍甩擊羅馬前線，羅馬以輕步兵、努米底亞騎兵與象兵反擊才守住營地，珀耳修斯損失三百人與二十四名「神聖」騎兵，羅馬營寨與輜重一度被奪，雙方未分勝負。公元前169年，珀耳修斯夜襲羅馬營寨，一度令全軍崩潰，羅馬靠集中起來的騎兵反擊才把營地守回來，這也是羅馬改派保利率領的關鍵背景。公元前168年6月22日的皮德納會戰是全役的樣本：拂曉羅馬軍出營，行軍數小時後接戰，兩翼各以約二千騎兵配置，中央是三段縱深、縱隊密集的步兵大隊，正面硬撼馬其頓方陣；羅馬中路一度被方陣推得後退，靠「劍盾如牆」的縱隊厚度頂住。真正的破口不在正面：方陣右翼的指揮官陣亡後，陣形露出縫隙，羅馬的輕步兵與弓手從兩側射擊暴露的側翼，羅馬騎兵隨即衝進方陣的側後；縱列一旦在側翼被射擊、被衝撞，就再也無法整齊地轉向，方陣於是崩成一群各自為戰的長矛手。追擊階段羅馬騎兵一路把殘兵趕到城牆下，馬其頓的戰列至此完全瓦解。羅馬全役的戰術核心其實是營寨制度：方形營地、壕溝、柵欄、按行軍序列紮營，讓遠征軍能在沒有補給線的山區裡待機三個戰役年，再以一次會戰決定戰爭。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the Third Macedonian War fall into three phases. In 171 BC the Roman army crossed the Adriatic; while marching through the Macedonian highlands its soldiers were bitten by wolves, which the army read as a bad omen, and the operation that actually set the tempo was the narrow defile of the Daynyls Pass, where the Roman column was strung out, the baggage train and the rearguard were harried by Macedonian light horse, and the Romans had to push straight through in a deep column covered by cavalry before they could open a road to the royal capital. Later the same year, at the river Callinicus, the Macedonians tried a newly invented dart thrown from a sling against the Roman front, and the Romans answered with light infantry, Numidian horse and elephants before recovering their camp; Perseus lost three hundred men and twenty-four of the 'sacred' cavalry, the Roman camp and baggage were overrun for a time, and the engagement was inconclusive. In 169 BC Perseus attacked the Roman camp by night and panicked it completely; the Romans recovered the position only by concentrating their cavalry and counterattacking, and that was the background to Rome's decision to send a different commander. The battle of Pydna on 22 June 168 BC is the model of the whole war: the Roman army marched out before dawn, walked for several hours and engaged about midday, with roughly two thousand cavalry on each wing and, in the centre, infantry maniples drawn up in three lines and in deep columns that collided head-on with the Macedonian phalanx; the Roman centre was pushed back for a time and held only by the thickness of the close-ordered column, in which shield and sword braced like a wall. The real breach was not frontal. When the commanders of the right wing of the phalanx were killed, gaps opened in the formation; Roman light infantry and archers shot into the exposed flanks, and the Roman cavalry charged into the flank and rear of the phalanx. Once a column on the flank is being shot at and ridden down it can no longer turn as a unit, and the phalanx dissolved into individual long-spear men fighting on their own. In the pursuit the Roman cavalry drove the broken troops to the city walls, and the Macedonian line was finished. The real tactical core of the Roman war effort, however, was the camp system: square camps, ditches, palisades, a marching camp laid out by the column of march, which allowed an expeditionary army to wait out three campaigning seasons in the mountains with no supply line and then to decide the war with a single pitched battle.
data: 關於兵員，各家記載互相矛盾，只能說個大概。能查到的最大一份編制是公元前171年珀耳修斯在基提翁集結的總兵力：步兵三萬九千，其中約半數是方陣重步兵，此外有克里特人三千、阿格里亞涅人與派奧尼亞人等三千、色雷斯人三千、高盧人二千；騎兵是馬其頓騎兵三千與色雷斯騎兵一千。公元前168年皮德納會戰，馬其頓方面步兵約二萬、騎兵六千，但因地形所限只有約三千騎兵能上陣；羅馬方面常見的說法是步兵約四萬、騎兵六千，波利比烏斯按戰場所見計的則是步兵二萬、騎兵二千出戰，其餘在營。會戰從拂曉行軍算起，到中午前後接戰，歷時約數小時。損失方面，史料記馬其頓軍損失二萬、被俘一萬一千，羅馬方面的傷亡不過百餘人、且多為佩利尼人，國王本人僅以數千騎兵突圍。戰役歷程：羅馬公元前171年出兵，168年6月22日皮德納決戰，167年元老院宣布馬其頓「自由」，從開戰到政治處理約四年。戰後安排有一組可核對的數字：馬其頓被分為四個自治區——安菲波利斯、帖撒利尼卡、佩拉與佩拉戈尼亞——羅馬抽走銀礦與銅礦收入，一千名貴族少年被召往羅馬充當人質，另有被列為「公敵」的馬其頓人遭處決，數目在後世記載中多作三千。戰利品方面，珀耳修斯的財貨大批運回羅馬，公元前167年塞爾維烏斯的凱旋式上首次出現大量青銅、象牙與金銀器，羅馬人此前只在傳說中見過這等排場。地理上，皮德納在奧林匹斯山西麓的皮埃里亞平原上，靠海而離羅馬的補給基地義利亞很遠，這正是遠征補給的主要難題。
dataEn: On numbers the ancient sources contradict one another, so only a rough picture is possible. The largest muster that can be checked is the army Perseus assembled at Citium in 171 BC: thirty-nine thousand foot, about half of them phalanx heavy infantry, together with three thousand Cretans, three thousand Agrianes, Paeonians and Parstrymonians, three thousand Thracians and two thousand Gauls; the horse was three thousand Macedonian cavalry and a thousand Thracian. At the battle of Pydna in 168 BC the Macedonians had about twenty thousand foot and six thousand horse, of whom only some three thousand could be brought into line because of the ground; the Roman figures commonly given are about forty thousand foot and six thousand horse, while Polybius, counting what was actually in the battle line, gives twenty thousand foot and two thousand cavalry engaged, the rest being in camp. The engagement ran from the march out of camp before dawn to contact around midday, a matter of several hours. On losses the sources record twenty thousand of the Macedonian army lost and eleven thousand taken prisoner, while the Romans lost no more than a hundred men, most of them Paelignians; the king himself escaped with only a few thousand horsemen. On duration: the Romans marched out in 171 BC, fought the decisive action at Pydna on 22 June 168, and the Senate declared Macedon 'free' in 167 BC, so roughly four years from the opening of hostilities to the political settlement. The settlement after the war has a set of checkable figures: Macedon was divided into four autonomous districts - Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella and Pelagonia - the Romans took the revenue of the silver and copper mines, one thousand young men of the nobility were summoned to Rome as hostages, and Macedonians previously declared enemies of the state were put to death, the number being given as three thousand in later accounts. As for booty, Perseus's treasure was carried back to Rome in bulk, and at the triumph of Servius in 167 BC crowds saw for the first time masses of bronze, ivory, gold and silver plate, a display Romans had previously known only from legend. Geographically Pydna lies on the plain of Pieria at the western foot of Mount Olympus, close to the sea and far from the Roman supply base at Brundisium, and that distance was the central logistical difficulty of the expedition.
cause: 導火線在塞琉古王國，不在馬其頓。公元前164年安提柯四世死，幼子安提奧庫斯五世被廢，長子德米特里二世與遠支亞歷山大·巴拉斯爭位，巴拉斯得到埃及托勒密六世承認；同一時期托勒密王朝也內鬥，托勒密八世在亞歷山大港弒兄奪位，埃及向羅馬求援。羅馬於是把自己擺上仲裁者的位置：公元前172年派出奧克塔維烏斯、梅魯拉與馬切多三名使團，赴塞琉古與埃及裁決。仲裁不利於德米特里二世，更不利於支持他的馬其頓人：羅馬裁定德米特里二世為塞琉古王，並否定珀耳修斯對塞琉古王位的一切主張。對馬其頓的「計算派」而言，這等於被判死刑，因為馬其頓的國策一向是維持在塞琉古與羅馬之間的中立並從中取利；對國王珀耳修斯而言，仲裁書不過是一份「待執行」的死刑令。公元前171年，他扣下使團、扣下兄弟德米特里、開放國境讓羅馬軍進入，試圖在談判桌上多換一點時間，同時向南方的塞琉古求援。真正的深層原因是羅馬的地中海戰略：安提柯四世曾打算重建塞琉古對希臘的霸權，甚至兵臨埃及，羅馬必須趁塞琉古內亂之際把希臘的勢力網拆掉，馬其頓是最容易被切下來的那一塊。開戰在羅馬看來是執行仲裁書，在馬其頓看來則是保衛國存。
causeEn: The trigger lay in the Seleucid Empire, not in Macedon. When Antiochus IV died in 164 BC his young son Antiochus V was set aside, and his elder son Demetrius II competed for the throne with a distant kinsman, Alexander Balas, who was acknowledged by Ptolemy VI of Egypt; at the same time the Ptolemaic kingdom was tearing itself apart, for Ptolemy VIII killed his brother in Alexandria and seized the Egyptian crown, and Egypt called on Rome for help. Rome then placed itself in the chair of the arbiter: in 172 BC it sent the envoys Octavius, Merula and Macedo to adjudicate between the Seleucid and the Egyptian claims. The award went against Demetrius II and, still more, against the Macedonians who had supported him: Rome recognised Demetrius II as Seleucid king and denied Perseus any claim to the Seleucid throne. For the 'calculating' party in Macedon this was tantamount to a death sentence, because Macedon's long policy had been to sit on the fence between Seleucid and Roman power and profit from it; for King Perseus the award was merely a death warrant awaiting execution. In 171 BC he detained the envoys, detained his own brother Demetrius, and opened his borders to the Roman army, buying time for further bargaining while also appealing south to the Seleucid court. The deeper cause lay in Roman strategy in the Mediterranean: Antiochus IV had sought to restore Seleucid hegemony over Greece and had even marched against Egypt, and Rome had to dismantle the Seleucid network in Greece while that empire was in civil war. Macedon was simply the piece that could be cut off most easily. To Rome the war was the execution of an award; to Macedon it was the defence of the state's existence.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果超出希臘。馬其頓王國就此滅亡，珀耳修斯成為最後一位國王；羅馬沒有扶植傀儡，而是宣布馬其頓「自由」，把它切成四個自治區，置總督，抽走銀、銅礦的開採權，並禁止各城邦自行結盟或鑄幣。塞琉古王國雖然保住了國體，卻從此再無能力與羅馬爭雄，東地中海出現了一個沒有對手的霸權，希臘城邦則被逐一編入羅馬的保護國體系。希臘人當時並不感激：失去主權的城邦把怨氣投向羅馬，埃托利亞同盟與其後的亞該亞同盟先後成為羅馬在希臘的敵人，最終引出公元前146年的科林斯戰役——同年迦太基與科林斯相繼陷落，羅馬取得地中海世界。到這個層面，第三次馬其頓戰爭是羅馬共和國晚期最大的一次擴張，它徹底解決了「誰來決定希臘命運」這個問題，答案不再是波斯、不是塞琉古、也不是馬其頓，而是羅馬。另一層次的後果在軍制：羅馬靠遠征與會戰累積的經驗，確立了執政官統率的常備遠征軍與配套的攻城工程；希臘化軍隊的技術——多族混編的方陣、弩砲、騎兵——同樣透過俘虜、逃亡者與被徵召的希臘工匠流入羅馬。武器史的旁證在亞洲：就在同一個世紀，秦軍正以弩兵在北疆築塹、壓制匈奴，弩機這種把力量儲存起來的機構，讓沒有受過長期拉弓訓練的兵也能在塹壕後面穩定射擊——與希臘人用弩砲壞城、羅馬用標槍壓制方陣，是同一條技術路線的兩端。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached beyond Greece. The kingdom of Macedon ceased to exist, with Perseus its last king; Rome did not install a puppet but declared Macedon 'free', cut it into four autonomous districts, placed it under governors, took the mining rights to the silver and copper, and forbade the cities to make alliances or coin money of their own. The Seleucid Empire survived as a state but never again possessed the strength to contest Roman supremacy, and there appeared in the eastern Mediterranean a power with no rival. The Greek cities were drawn one by one into the Roman system of client states, and they were not grateful: the loss of autonomy turned their resentment against Rome, and the Aetolian League and after it the Achaean League became Rome's enemies in Greece, ending in the Roman war against Corinth in 146 BC, the same year in which Carthage and Corinth fell and Rome acquired the Mediterranean world. At that level the Third Macedonian War was the largest single expansion of the late Roman republic: it settled the question of who would decide the fate of Greece, and the answer was no longer Persia, nor the Seleucids, nor Macedon, but Rome. A second layer of consequence lies in military organisation: Rome's accumulation of experience in distant campaigns and in pitched battle established the standing expeditionary army commanded by a consul together with the engineering that supported it; the techniques of the Hellenistic armies - the mixed phalanx of many nations, the catapult, the cavalry - flowed into Rome through prisoners, deserters and conscripted Greek craftsmen. The parallel in the history of weapons lies in Asia: in the same century the Qin army was massing crossbowmen behind ramparts on the northern frontier to hold down the Xiongnu, and the crossbow, by storing the drawn power, let troops with no long training in the bow fire steadily from behind a ditch - the other end of the same technical line on which the Greeks broke cities with artillery and the Romans broke phalanxes with the pilum.
result: 公元前168年6月22日皮德納的會戰決定了戰局。馬其頓方陣在正面沒有崩，崩在側翼：國王之子菲力普與其弟德米特里相繼陣亡，騎兵指揮官米尼翁被衝散，珀耳修斯本人只帶數千騎兵突圍，退往王都佩拉與海港。羅馬隨即封鎖馬其頓沿岸，珀耳修斯走投無路，經山道逃到薩莫色雷斯島，在島上被羅馬海軍指揮官奧克塔維烏斯接住——這位將領數年前還曾以賓客身分住在國王的宮廷裏，卻仍然受命接管囚徒。珀耳修斯於公元前168年投降，翌年被押往羅馬，失去王位與自由，軟禁中病亡。公元前167年，羅馬元老院正式宣布馬其頓「自由」：王國廢除，土地分為四個自治區（安菲波利斯、帖撒利尼卡、佩拉與佩拉戈尼亞），各區雖設議會，向羅馬繳納的貢賦卻只有舊日付給國王的一半，馬其頓全國議會亦被解散，國庫與礦場被接收，青年貴族被召往羅馬，一批被列為公敵者遭處決。戰爭以羅馬共和國的完全勝利告終：它沒有在戰場上取走珀耳修斯的性命，卻奪走了馬其頓這個國家、塞琉古稱霸希臘的可能，以及希臘人自己決定自身命運的餘地。塞爾維烏斯的凱旋式把戰利品陳列於羅馬街頭，第三次馬其頓戰爭也就此落幕，第四次馬其頓戰爭在二十多年後仍會再起，直到公元前146年希臘的自由被最終取消。
resultEn: The battle of Pydna on 22 June 168 BC decided the war. The Macedonian phalanx did not break in front; it broke on the flank. The king's son Philippus and his brother Demetrius were killed in turn, the cavalry commander Minnion was scattered, and Perseus himself escaped with a few thousand horsemen, falling back towards the royal capital Pella and the harbour. Rome then blockaded the Macedonian coast, and with no way out Perseus took a mountain road to the island of Samothrace, where he was taken in by the Roman naval commander Gnaeus Octavius - the general who not long before had been a guest in the king's own court, and who nevertheless received the order to take the prisoner. Perseus surrendered in 168 BC and was brought to Rome the following year, stripped of his kingship and of his freedom, and he died of illness while under guard. In 167 BC the Roman Senate formally declared Macedon 'free': the kingdom was abolished, the land divided into four autonomous districts - Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella and Pelagonia - each keeping its own council but paying Rome a tribute only half of what used to be paid to the king, the national council of Macedon being dissolved, the treasury and the mines taken over, the young nobles summoned to Rome, and a number of those declared enemies of the state executed. The war ended in a complete Roman victory. It did not take Perseus's life in the field, but it took the state of Macedon, the possibility of Seleucid primacy in Greece, and the margin by which the Greeks might have decided their own fate. Servius's triumph displayed the booty in the streets of Rome, and with it the Third Macedonian War came to its close; the Fourth Macedonian War would break out more than twenty years later, until in 146 BC the freedom of Greece was cancelled for good.
